title: Stunt Car Racer
build: MicroStyle release for PAL machines, the C64 Preservation Project G64 (SHA-1 0540264fca9bd8583c4bfcc9a6f422b2ac25f5c9), uncracked; one load after its own loader

tools.host: Linux x86_64 cloud container, no display

accuracy.note: 18 more comments that shared the mistakes corrected with them
the comments on the Super League's race settings at $BFEA and $BFF6 corrected when the features were checked against the code

every routine ported and checked against the game's code on random states and in lockstep from the loader's hand-over (four sessions of 1,000 passes, every byte of memory, colour RAM and the chips identical at each pass); the port and the comments were written together, group by group, so the corrections are the sample's

exclude: not loaded: zero page, the stack, pages 2 to 7 and $0800-$083F are the game's variables and buffers (the track's pieces at $0400-$07FF, the KERNAL's vectors kept at $0800), all set at run time; the start-up's checksum (checksum_ranges, $42A9) starts at $0840, and at the hand-over these hold what the loader left
not loaded: the bitmap at $4000 past the start-up, where the 3D view and the menus are drawn; the checksum leaves it out, and at the hand-over it holds zeros and, from $4307, bytes the loader left
not loaded: rows of the bitmap at $4000 between the tables at $4F00 and $5780; the checksum leaves them out, and at the hand-over they hold the RAM's power-on pattern
not loaded: the league's 192 bytes, made by NEW_LEAGUE and saved and loaded with a game; the checksum leaves them out, and at the hand-over they hold the RAM's power-on pattern
not loaded: work tables the game fills while it runs; the checksum leaves them out, and at the hand-over they hold the RAM's power-on pattern

not loaded: the tables the start-up copies here from the bitmaps' area (described where they are loaded, at $5780 and $63E0-$7648) and the game's variables from $C300; the checksum leaves them out, and at the hand-over they are zeros
not loaded: the processor's vectors, which the start-up sets ($FFFA the NMI's, $FFFE the interrupt's), and zeros; the checksum ends at $FFE1
include: loaded with the game: the race's screen, its first two colours for each cell of the bitmaps, and the sprite pointers; the menus refill it (FILL_SCREEN)
